ahorn.text: Ahorn has been at this since 2012, and the years show in the best way: comfortable in the upper reaches, quick-handed, and rarely rattled when the opposition stiffens. The lifetime board paints a slightly taller picture than the matchups do, and against the toughest third the edge softens a little. Read this one as a sketch of a long, solid career: the opponent sample behind it is older and smaller.

averagecpopenjoyer.text: AverageCPOPenjoyer is a young account with an old hand's game: upper tier on the matchup board, fast hands, and unbothered when the opposition stiffens. When the opposition gets toughest, the edge frays a little, the only soft spot so far. Early read, but the opening already carries weight.

alandwhalens.text: ALandWhaleNS plays a powerful, patient game: matchup rating, activity, and resistance all among the very best, with a brisk pace behind them. The accuracy sits at the very top, though the hardest third takes a little of the edge off. An older, smaller opponent sample stands behind this one, so take it as a sketch rather than a portrait.

amatelass.text: AMATELASS chooses the moment, then holds the ground: matchup rating and resistance both among the very best, with a matchup kill-death line to match. The bravery number is low, which fits a player who waits for the right opening instead of chasing every fight. The lifetime board sells the whole picture far too short, with the lifetime IvI far below what the matchups support.

aekris.text: Aekris waits on high ground and bursts into fights other people already started, almost never taking a fair one-on-one: ranks with the highest tracked on the matchup board, precise of aim, and unbothered as fights harden. The numbers fade as the opposition strengthens: the approach is picking the moment, not grinding through every fight. Facing the strongest third, the form thins, the single weak spot in an otherwise sharp sheet.

alandwhalenc.text: ALandWhaleNC plays a patient, punishing game: belongs in the top tier across nearly every measure, a rapid tempo, and unwavering as fights harden. Activity fades as the opposition strengthens. The play is all about the right moment, not every fight. The form falls away sharply against the strongest third, the one soft spot in an otherwise sharp record.

alandwhaletr.text: ALandWhaleTR has played since 2018, and the record shows it: stands near the head of the board throughout nearly every measure, a high tempo, and steady as the opposition hardens. The output holds as the opposition strengthens. That strength holds against the strongest opposition. The career numbers back the matchups, no gap between them.

artofdying.text: Artofdying has played since 2014, and the record shows it: sits among the best tracked in nearly every measure, a swift tempo, and collected as fights harden. The output stays strong as the opposition strengthens. The edge holds against the hardest third. Lifetime and matchup boards paint the same picture.

alandwhale.text: ALandWhale has been at this since 2015 and still plays at the summit: among the very best tracked, the matchup kill-death mark near the top and output holding mid-pack as foes get stronger. The toughest-third hold sinks low, the one soft spot. Take this as a sketch: it rests on an older, smaller opponent sample.

arneen.text: Arneen is a young account with a cool head for timing: among the very best tracked already, picking the moment and then winning it, with aim that rarely misses. The output never chases stronger opposition, and the toughest-third hold slips a touch. Early read, but the opening pages are loud.

art0fdying.text: Art0fdying plays the long, patient game from the summit: sitting with the very best tracked, winning fights at a measured tempo while the matchup kill-death numbers run near the top. The output holds firm as the opposition improves. The strongest-third hold stays high. On the board since 2014, and still at the very top.

averagejpopenjoyer.text: averageJPOPenjoyer is a young account playing a complete game: top shelf on nearly every count, a trigger that stays hot, and an edge that holds as the bar rises. The kept share stays high against the strongest third too. Early read, but the opening already carries weight.

angrylendoria.text: AngryLendoria picks the moment and then makes it count: in the upper echelon, with a matchup kill-death ratio among the very best on the board. The bravery line sits near the bottom, which means the fights are chosen, not stumbled into, and the line holds against harder foes, though the edge fades a little against the strongest third. The lifetime board is split: the kill-death line agrees with the matchups, while the IvI line sits near the very bottom.

aimbot.text: Aimbot plays a polished, high-volume game: elite on every line, with pace at the very top and a game that rises with the opposition. The aim is precise, though the headshots are rare and the lifetime IvI lands mid-pack. The consistency mark dips below average, the one soft spot in an otherwise strong card.

artemiync.text: ArtemiyNC fights with a surgeon's patience: top shelf in the matchups, precise, and still dangerous as foes get stronger. The edge thins against the hardest third, the one soft spot on the card. The public board undersells this one a little: its IvI line sits a notch below the matchup rating.

artemiyvs.text: ArtemiyVS plays a measured, deliberate game: top shelf in the matchups, exact, and hard to shake as foes get stronger. Against the hardest third the edge wears thin, the single soft spot on the card. Take this one as a sketch drawn from an older, smaller opponent sample.

abisme.text: Abisme plays a patient, measured game: ranked top shelf, with the matchup kill-death figures up near the top. The tempo sits above average, the aim sits mid-table, and the lifetime IvI number trails a little behind. Nothing flashy, just a strong regular doing the work.

athleticquest.text: AthleticQuest plays a balanced, busy game: sitting top shelf, with a blistering pace and daring baked in. The edge holds up against the hardest third too, while the lifetime ledger keeps pace with the matchups, while the aim stays steady. A strong regular, quietly getting the work done.

aaeatieati.text: AAeatieati brings the full package: matchup rating and activity both up at the very top, with bravery in step and a rhythm that never fades. The accuracy sits near the top, the headshot share sits there too, and the lifetime IvI sits among the very best too. A player who shows up sharp in every corner of the card.

activaterogue.text: ActivateRogue has been winning the same way since 2014: a matchup rating near the top, resistance to match, and a kill-death mark in those matchups that sits among the very best tracked. The lifetime kill-death board agrees, placing the career at the very peak, while the lifetime IvI sits mid-pack — the matchups tell the stronger story. The aim is middling, the headshot share ordinary, yet the results keep coming.

anjaneeyre.text: ANJaneEyre brings thunder: the adjusted rating leads the card, the tempo crackles, the nerve holds, the staying power never wavers. The matchup kill-death mark keeps pace, and a lifetime kill-death board sits near the peak. Headshots are rare and the lifetime IvI rests mid-pack, so the matchups rate this game above the lifetime ledger. Consistency slips below average — the lone crack in an otherwise commanding card.

arraino.text: Arraino does not waste motion: activity near the top, bravery and resistance right there with it, and a matchup kill-death mark among the very best tracked. The pace is fierce, the aim lands near the top, and headshots land often. The lifetime board agrees on every count, carrying the career near the summit.

auntmcthy.text: AuntMcthy turns every fight into a statement: the adjusted rating crowns the card, the tempo never lets up, courage holds against stronger enemies, and the staying power matches it. The kill-death mark in those matchups follows suit. The pace is relentless, the aim rarely misses, and the lifetime board agrees, rating the whole career in the top ranks. Nothing here leans on soft opposition — the game holds up however the opposition shapes up.

averagekpopenjoyer.text: averageKPOPenjoyer leaves nothing to chance: every line on the card sits near the top, from matchup rating and bravery to resistance, pace, accuracy, and headshot share. The lifetime ledger agrees, putting the career near the summit, and the matchup kill-death mark backs it up. A complete, high-tempo game with no soft corner anywhere.

arabskoesaltoparcourparcouuur.text: ArabskoeSaltoParcourParcouuur plays every line at the top: rating, activity, bravery, resistance, and matchup kill-death all near the very summit, with a brisk kill pace and precise aim. The headshot share lands near the top and the lifetime board agrees. Only consistency dips below average — a single wrinkle on a veteran's card that has held strong since 2018.

atzeb.text: AtzeB has been around since 2013 and fights like someone who has seen every trick: bravery near the very bottom, yet resistance among the very best and a matchup kill-death mark to match. The pace stays middling, the headshots land near the top, and the consistency holds firm against the strongest third. A veteran who chooses the moment with enormous care — and usually wins it.

akaruby.text: Akaruby plays a sharp, patient game: tempo in the top ranks, bravery comfortably above average, and resistance up near the very top. The matchup kill-death mark ranks among the best tracked, headshots land at a strong rate, and the lifetime board places them among the best too. Consistency dips against the hardest opposition, the one soft line on a strong card.

arunvix.text: Arunvix is the straight line at the top: matchup rating, pace, bravery, aim — every measure but one lands in the upper tier. The lifetime ledger agrees, rating them near the top too, and resistance unmoved by the hardest attacks. Consistency sits mid-pack, the one soft note in an otherwise spotless card. A fighter with almost nothing left to prove and no sign of slowing down.

aerialanomalies.text: AerialAnomalies plays a careful, deadly hand: one of the highest marks tracked, with matchup kill-death figures near the top and resistance among the very best. The tempo is middling and headshots are scarce, yet the results stay elite on body-shot precision alone. The lifetime IvI sits mid-pack, so the matchups put them well clear of the lifetime board.

anas97.text: anas97 has been carving through the same battlefields since 2013, and the years show in the composure: a matchup rating near the top, a matchup kill-death mark among the very best, and resistance that barely bends against stronger opposition. The tempo sits well above average without ever looking rushed, and the lifetime board agrees the whole picture is strong. A veteran who still wins the fights that matter.

angrylendorianc.text: AngryLendoriaNC plays like a storm front: activity and matchup kill-death marks near the very top, resistance that holds against the toughest opposition, and a lifetime kill-death ratio among the very best. The headshot share sits below average, which only underlines that the kills come from relentless pressure rather than pinpoint headshots. A veteran since 2018, still setting the pace.

asterixthelegionary.text: AsterixTheLegionary has carried this standard since 2018: rating, tempo, bravery, resistance — all four adjusted lines in the upper tier, where the matchup kill-death mark stands right there with them. The aim is top-shelf on both counts, accuracy and headshot share alike. Consistency sits below average — the edge softens against the strongest third — yet the lifetime numbers still land in the upper tier, a veteran's card through and through.

almosthonest.text: AlmostHonest plays a straight, relentless game: the matchup grade sits near the summit, the tempo matches that height, and the game holds up as the enemies get stronger, with a brisk kill rate and the kill-death mark well above average. Accuracy sits near the top and headshots make up a top share of the hits, while the lifetime ledger lands in the same high bracket. A veteran since 2016, still sharp on every line.

andrey25rus.text: Andrey25rus brings heat on every line: the tempo, the game against stronger enemies, and the kill-death mark all sit near the top, with kills coming quickly and the matchup rating up there too. Shots land true, with headshots clearing well above average. The lifetime ledger runs in the same strong range. Consistency dips below average, the lone blemish on an otherwise strong card.

andrey25rusvs.text: Andrey25rusVS plays at full tilt: the tempo runs near the very top, the game keeps its edge against tougher enemies, and the matchup rating lands in the same range. The aim stays precise, with headshots well above average. Lifetime numbers track in the same high range. Consistency sags below average, the lone soft line on an otherwise strong card.

almax01.text: almax01 wins by patience: a matchup mark near the top built on resistance that barely bends, with headshots near the very top. The work rate sits in the middle, the accuracy does too, and the results stay elite anyway. The lifetime board trails the matchups by a step, which only sharpens the picture of a player who waits for the right moment.

alyrisa.text: Alyrisa is a scalpel, not a bludgeon: accuracy near the top, a matchup kill-death mark near the very top, and resistance to match. Bravery sits in the middle, and the consistency mark lands near the bottom, so the results lean on shot selection more than staying power. A veteran since 2013 whose lifetime board sits well below the matchups.
